title: What Investment Funds Are and How They Work
summary: The basic idea of pooled investment, how a fund turns investors' money into a managed portfolio, and why investors choose funds over direct investment.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The basic idea of pooled investment, how a fund turns investors' money into a managed portfolio, and why investors choose funds over direct investment.
Learning Objectives: Describe an investment fund and the pooling of investor money
Explain the benefits of diversification, professional management and scale
Identify the main types of investor and how they access funds
Syllabus: Pooled investment, units, shares and net asset value
Why investors subscribe: diversification, expertise, liquidity and cost
Access routes: direct, platforms, advisers and wrappers
Intended Audience: New joiners and graduates at fund managers, administrators, depositaries, transfer agents, law firms and distributors
Staff of supervisory authorities joining fund supervision or authorisation teams
Professionals moving into the funds industry from banking, audit or other sectors who need a complete foundation
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of investment funds is required. A general awareness of financial markets is helpful.
Core Reading: IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
IOSCO (2013), Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes
IOSCO (2018), Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes
FSB (2017), Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Asset Management Activities
